title: MLPC 01 - Introduction to Classification
subject: Machine Learning and Pattern Classification
description: Covers the classification pipeline, features, decision boundaries, generalisation, overfitting, and learning paradigms. All questions are single-choice and modeled after the conceptual style of the MLPC Retry 2024S exam. Source: 01_Introduction_to_Class.pdf.

questions.question: A fish classifier receives raw camera images. Which step is specifically responsible for turning each image into measurements such as length, width, and lightness?

options.text: Classification
Feature extraction
Cost-sensitive evaluation
Model selection

questions.explanation: Feature extraction reduces raw data to informative measurements used by the classifier.

questions.question: A fish is represented by lightness and width. What is the correct geometric interpretation?

options.text: It is a class label in a two-class set
It is a point in a two-dimensional feature space
It is a decision boundary
It is a probability distribution

questions.explanation: A vector of two feature values identifies one point in a two-dimensional feature space.

questions.question: A length threshold misclassifies some salmon and sea bass because their length distributions overlap. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: No classifier can solve the task
Length alone is not a perfect discriminator
The labels must be incorrect
The threshold must equal the mean fish length

questions.explanation: Overlap means no single threshold on length can perfectly separate the classes.

questions.question: Misclassifying sea bass as salmon is made much more costly than the reverse error. What should a minimum-risk designer generally consider?

options.text: Moving the decision boundary to reduce the expensive error
Keeping the boundary fixed because accuracy is unchanged
Removing all sea bass examples
Using only the cheapest class as training data

questions.explanation: Unequal costs can justify shifting the boundary even if the total number of errors changes.

questions.question: A highly curved boundary makes zero errors on a small training set, while a simpler boundary makes two errors. Which model is guaranteed to perform better on future fish?

options.text: The curved model
The simple model
Both perform identically
Neither is guaranteed from training error alone

questions.explanation: Training fit alone does not determine generalisation; the complex model may be overfitting.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a learned classifier?

options.text: Memorise the labels of training examples
Correctly classify new cases from the application domain
Maximise the number of features
Create the most complex possible boundary

questions.explanation: The goal is generalisation to new, unseen cases, not merely remembering the training set.

questions.question: Which change most directly increases the expressive complexity of a two-feature classifier?

options.text: Replacing a curved boundary with a straight line
Allowing more complex decision boundaries
Reducing the number of training examples
Ignoring one of the two features

questions.explanation: A richer family of boundaries can represent more complicated class regions.

questions.question: Which description best matches classical machine learning in the lecture's comparison of learning paradigms?

options.text: Hand-write both features and decision rules
Hand-design a feature extractor, then train a classifier
Learn every stage end-to-end from raw input
Use no labeled examples

questions.explanation: Classical ML commonly uses engineered features followed by a learned classifier.

questions.question: Which description best matches end-to-end deep learning?

options.text: The feature extractor and classifier are learned jointly from input to output
Only the final threshold is learned
All rules are written manually
Training labels are unnecessary in every case

questions.explanation: End-to-end systems optimise a stack of functions, often learning features and classification jointly.

questions.question: Which property is most desirable for training and test data in a real classification project?

options.text: They should contain only easy examples
They should be representative, correctly labeled, and sufficiently large
They should contain as many duplicated examples as possible
They should be selected after seeing the classifier's mistakes

questions.explanation: Representative and reliable data are required for learning and meaningful evaluation.
